quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on OKC Thunder getting punched in the mouth twice
quotes.excerpt: I've never seen OKC get punched in the mouth twice in one series as hard as they got punched.

text_blocks.speaker: Paul Pierce
text_blocks.text: I've never seen OKC get punched in the mouth twice in one series as hard as they got punched, ever. In the last two years, the way how dominant they've been, nobody is winning there at their building or OKC on the road. And just put them on their knee, twice.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: AI knew somehow even the NBA is going to be ruined and corrupted by artificial intelligence just like the rest of the world.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: It's hard to do because those teams are going to be healthy, but again, if the Knicks don't get it this year, it's OKC and San Antonio in the next five years.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the public's negative perception of the OKC Thunder
quotes.excerpt: People were happy when the Warriors lost to the Cavs, bro. That's my point.

text_blocks.speaker: Paul Pierce
text_blocks.text: People were happy when the Warriors lost to the Cavs, bro. That's my point. If they win one, and they start dominating next year, nobody is going to like it. Nobody is going to enjoy it. People like it now. They like, oh, we hate, we hate, um, OKC, so let's root for the most unfair player ever.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: He's like, he's a 7-foot Steph Curry.

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: When he starts acting, no, listen, when you start becoming the money maker, he's going to be, they're going to hate Steph specifically.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on why players skip media availability after losses
quotes.excerpt: Most guys are more likely to skip after a loss after they get beat.
quotes.quote: Most guys are more likely to skip after a loss after they get beat. And sometimes they protect you because he might have been in an emotional state, and they might have not wanted him to say something in the press conference that would be detrimental to himself and also the group. So they probably just said, yo, we're just going to hold them away for right now.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on San Antonio creating doubt in the OKC locker room
quotes.excerpt: I believe San Antonio created a little doubt in OKC's locker room.
quotes.quote: I believe San Antonio created a little doubt in OKC's locker room, because they're like, damn, how does a team go on a 20-0 run? You thinking like, Shai, I'm struggling, how can I score? It's frustrating. They're not going to be able to sleep. And if I'm San Antonio, I'm like, we better than them, y'all. Y'all see this? We better than them.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on choosing between a back-to-back MVP and Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: Who would you rather have, the back-to-back MVP or Victor Wembanyama?
quotes.quote: Who would you rather have, the back-to-back MVP or Victor Wembanyama? It's a great question. Most years, this will be a no-brainer. The back-to-back MVP, no doubt. Right? But then you look at this dude, and you're like, damn. Especially coming off of the Game 6, the Game 6 that he had.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on Victor Wembanyama's need for easier baskets
quotes.excerpt: What's he going to do when those shots are not falling? How is he going to get easier baskets?
quotes.quote: What's he going to do when those shots are not falling? How is he going to get easier baskets? How is he, because like if you're not knocking that three down early in the game, then like what are you going to go to? You know, like are you establishing yourself at the free throw line, having a dominant free throw night? You know, are you being dominant on the defensive, in which he can control?

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on the direct correlation between rebounds and activity
quotes.excerpt: The rebound is a direct correlation to his activity.
quotes.quote: The rebound is a direct correlation to his activity. If he's not making shots, and he doesn't get more than eight rebounds because, said, when he gets more than eight rebounds, they're eight and two now. When he's less than eight rebounds, they're two and four. You know what I'm saying? Like he's got 10 rebounds, is he going to get blocked shots? Is he going to rebound the ball? Is he going to get closer to the basket to get his own shot?

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on Jalen Brunson's lack of lift and confidence
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson, he looked like a guy that was lacking lift, lacking confidence in the shot.
quotes.quote: Jalen Brunson, he looked like a guy that was lacking lift, lacking confidence in the shot, in the handle. Obviously he's coming back from a severe injury. Like you don't miss all of this time in the most important segment of the season against a team that is a whale of a team if you're not severely injured. We know that he's dealing with physical ailments, but like to watch him play tonight, it was rough.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on Victor Wembanyama's potential as a defensive player
quotes.excerpt: We are already witnessing one of the greatest defensive players we've ever seen.
quotes.quote: We are already witnessing one of the greatest defensive players we've ever seen. Did you hear what I just said? Ever. Like on the court. There's no denying about that. So, I think he goes under.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the Knicks' defensive performance in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: They're playing better than anybody in the playoffs right now.
quotes.quote: They're playing better than anybody in the playoffs right now. And you got to put in the equation that these two teams are beating each other for seven games, and then they're going to, but at the same time they'll be able to stay home. I think if you're beating each other up for seven games, you have to go on the road, that makes a major difference. But they'll be home for a few days before the finals start, which is great.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the NBA using AI for officiating
quotes.excerpt: The league will use AI to automate a category of calls such as out-of-bounds decisions.
quotes.quote: The league will use AI to automate a category of calls such as out-of-bounds decisions to speed up games and reduce disputes over possession. We're going to move to a system like that where that whole category of calls will be automatic. It will take all those so-called objective calls out of the hands of the referees. You won't have to deal with challenges on those calls.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul Pierce on the human element of officiating
quotes.excerpt: Human error was part of the game. Everybody understands this.
quotes.quote: Human error was part of the game. Everybody understands this. Like it's part of it. Like the refs have to have some level of discretion and discernment. And like, yeah, Tony Brothers' calls are different from Steve Javie, but like that's kind of part of the game that everybody understands. This whole like, let's make it uniform and robotic, I don't know.
